description: One room and most of it is bench. A cast-iron last stand with five lasts on it in a row by size, a finishing wheel on a countershaft under the bench that he starts with his knee, and a wall of every colour of thread and every gauge of tack in little drawers that are labelled in a hand nobody else could read. Repairs waiting on a shelf in pairs, each with a paper tag through the laces. The smell is leather, wax and the particular hot-dust smell of a wheel that has been running. There is one chair for a customer and it faces the bench, deliberately, so you watch.

window.description: The bench window, low and wide, set at the height of the work rather than the height of a person. From inside it frames the pavement from the knee down, which after a while tells you more about who is coming than a face would.
window.name: the bench window

name: Sole Survivor — The Bench
